content: The purpose of screening for nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is to identify individuals who are at an increased risk of developing adverse health outcomes associated with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). These outcomes include cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and liver-related mortality. The risk of these complications is particularly elevated in individuals who have central obesity, cardiometabolic risk factors, or insulin resistance. However, there are limitations to relying solely on insulin resistance and cardiometabolic factors as surrogate markers for screening, as their predictive value may vary. For example, hypertension has a lower specificity for identifying insulin resistance. Additionally, certain populations, such as young adults and lean individuals, may exhibit steatosis and insulin resistance even in the absence of traditional cardiometabolic risk factors.
